package_info.package_versions: prior to 2.4.8-0ubuntu2.1 (patched June 2024), specifically Ubuntu 24.04 LTS default
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a logic flaw in the handling of UNIX domain socket permissions, allowing an attacker to escalate privileges by exploiting a sequence of configuration changes and symlink attacks, ultimately leading to arbitrary root code execution. The vulnerability is not due to intentionally malicious code, but the resulting behavior enables privilege escalation and arbitrary command execution as root.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the cups daemon is restarted via the ServerSetSettings DBus method, the Listen parameter is set to a symlink under attacker control, causing cupsd to perform a chmod 777 on the symlink target (/etc/cups/cupsd.conf), making it world-writable.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Changing a privileged configuration file to be world-writable via a symlink is a classic privilege escalation technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal configuration changes should not allow a non-root user to make privileged files world-writable or manipulate symlinks to escalate privileges.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Listen directives are used to configure socket paths, but not to escalate privileges or change file permissions on unrelated files.
key_indicators: Symlink from unprivileged location to privileged file

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After gaining write access to cupsd.conf, the attacker adds a Listen directive pointing to a symlink to /etc/cups/cups-files.conf. On the next restart, cupsd performs chmod 777 on /etc/cups/cups-files.conf, making it world-writable.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Chaining symlink attacks to escalate from one privileged file to another is a hallmark of privilege escalation exploits.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Configuration files should not be writable by unprivileged users, nor should configuration changes allow arbitrary file permission changes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Listen directives are for socket configuration, not for manipulating unrelated file permissions.
key_indicators: World-writable permissions on privileged config files

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The attacker sets the Group parameter in cups-files.conf to 'netdev', causing all external programs executed by cups (such as print filters) to run with group netdev privileges.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Changing the group for external program execution to a group with elevated privileges (netdev) is a privilege escalation step.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal users should not be able to change the execution group for privileged daemons.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Changing the group may be legitimate for system administrators, but not for unprivileged users.
key_indicators: Modification of execution context for privileged processes
Escalation to a group with special DBus permissions

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a print job is submitted to the attacker-controlled printer, the FoomaticRIPCommandLine executes an attacker-supplied Python script as the group netdev.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abusing the print filter command line to execute arbitrary code is a classic code injection technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: PPD files should not allow unprivileged users to execute arbitrary code as privileged groups.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom print filters may be used by admins, but not for arbitrary code execution.
key_indicators: Arbitrary command execution via print job

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when print job is processed by cups)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import dbus
bus = dbus.SystemBus()
wpasup = bus.get_object('fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1', '/fi/w1/wpa_supplicant1')
wpasup.CreateInterface({'ConfigFile': '/tmp/stage/wpa.conf'})
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script calls the wpa_supplicant's CreateInterface DBus method, passing a configuration file that references an attacker-controlled shared object, triggering wpa_supplicant (running as root) to load and execute attacker code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abusing DBus interfaces to trigger privileged daemons to load attacker-controlled code is a sophisticated privilege escalation technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal print jobs should not interact with network configuration daemons or load arbitrary shared objects.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be network configuration by system tools, not by print jobs.
key_indicators: DBus call to privileged service from print filter

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
opensc_engine_path=/tmp/stage/libpayload.so
# libpayload.so contains a constructor that sets /usr/bin/python3 to setuid root
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When wpa_supplicant loads the configuration, it loads the attacker-supplied shared object, which executes code as root (e.g., sets /usr/bin/python3 to setuid root), enabling persistent root shell access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading arbitrary shared objects from untrusted locations is a critical security flaw, especially when the code runs as root.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: wpa_supplicant should only load trusted, system-provided shared objects.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate plugins/extensions, but only from trusted paths.

attack_chain.action: Create symlink from /tmp/stage/cupsd.conf to /etc/cups/cupsd.conf and use DBus ServerSetSettings to set Listen to this path.
Modify /etc/cups/cupsd.conf to add Listen /tmp/stage/cups-files.conf (symlink to /etc/cups/cups-files.conf), then trigger another ServerSetSettings call.
Set Group netdev in /etc/cups/cups-files.conf to ensure external programs run as group netdev.
attack_chain.leads_to: Print filters run as group netdev

attack_chain.action: Install a printer with a PPD file containing a FoomaticRIPCommandLine that executes an attacker-controlled Python script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution as group netdev

attack_chain.action: Submit a print job to trigger the Python script, which calls wpa_supplicant's CreateInterface method with a config referencing an attacker-controlled shared object.
attack_chain.leads_to: wpa_supplicant loads attacker-controlled shared object as root

attack_chain.action: wpa_supplicant loads the shared object, which sets /usr/bin/python3 to setuid root, enabling root shell access.

behavioral_signatures: Repeated DBus calls to org.opensuse.cupspkhelper ServerSetSettings with Listen parameters pointing to symlinks
Unexpected changes to Group parameter in cups-files.conf (especially to netdev)
Installation of printers with PPD files containing FoomaticRIPCommandLine executing non-standard binaries/scripts
Print jobs triggering execution of scripts or binaries outside standard print filters
DBus calls to wpa_supplicant's CreateInterface from non-network management processes
wpa_supplicant loading shared objects from non-standard paths (e.g., /tmp, /home, /var/tmp)
file_indicators: PPD files with FoomaticRIPCommandLine referencing /tmp or user-writable locations
network_indicators: DBus traffic to org.opensuse.cupspkhelper and fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1 from non-standard clients
Unusual DBus method calls (ServerSetSettings, PrinterAddWithPpdFile, CreateInterface) from user sessions
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for DBus calls to org.opensuse.cupspkhelper with Listen parameters pointing to symlinks or non-standard paths, and for repeated changes to cups configuration files' permissions. Alert on world-writable permissions set on /etc/cups/cupsd.conf or /etc/cups/cups-files.conf. Flag any PPD files with FoomaticRIPCommandLine executing scripts or binaries outside standard print filters. Monitor wpa_supplicant for attempts to load shared objects from non-system directories (e.g., /tmp, /home). Correlate print job submissions with subsequent DBus calls to wpa_supplicant and changes to setuid binaries (e.g., /usr/bin/python3).
